svg.text: F Sub-mechanisms (5) — spinning, rinsing, peeling, and two rejects
Each panel loops on its own.
source: F-first-principles.md section 6
S23 reel-through: see F-tuch; S24 revolver wash: see F-saeule
S47 Spin-coat
Pan on a rotating mount. At 500 rpm a dough disc might open
like a thrown pizza (unverified; centre thins first).
Feasibility M for batter, L for dough
S25 Spin-dry everything
Spin the rack instead of blowing hot air: replaces most of the
15–20 min drying step. Rotary tools dry themselves the same way.
Feasibility H
S42 Deglaze-rinse

g.text: rinse the emptied bowl with the recipe's own stock
and send it to the pot

svg.text: Yield goes up, the soil load of the wash goes down.
Works for bowls, trays and the mat.
Feasibility H
S10 Iris peeler (industrial type)
As industrial carrot and asparagus peelers; six pivots to keep clean
(compare the one-piece flexure version, E-S9).
Feasibility M–H
S29 Mini flat-bed breader

g.text: vibrating tray: 100 g crumbs as bed + curtain

svg.text: A true bed needs 1.5 L of crumbs for one cutlet, and raw meat
contaminates it after one batch.
Listed so it can be rejected knowingly
S30 Vacuum wand for granules
Pellet conveying as in plastics plants: no box tilting — but every
metre of hose is a Zone F surface nobody can see or wash.
Feasibility L; listed so it can be rejected knowingly
